title: Chapter 70: Special Visitor
html:
The Midnight Ticket Counter is broken, but there’s no obvious way to repair it. The black phone keeps giving me the strangest things.

Chen Ge climbed out of the booth. The longer he studied it, the more certain he became that it had not been built for the living.

“Boss!” Xu Wan jogged toward him in her casual outfit, holding two steaming buns in her hands.

The sight of cheerful Xu Wan immediately lifted Chen Ge’s mood. She could be a little oblivious, but her natural warmth brightened even the gloomiest day.

Chen Ge accepted her offering and happily bit into the bun. “Why are you here so early?”

“Boss, look!” Xu Wan sat beside him on the steps and pulled out her phone. A long list of articles and videos covered the Ping An Apartments case. “They’re all about you. Boss, you’re famous!”

“Let me see.” Chen Ge looked at the articles, not expecting the short interview from the day before to have gone viral. “Such a waste.”

“Waste? Why? I think it’s wonderful.” Xu Wan’s face was flushed, probably from her short run.

“I was so focused on the reward money that I forgot what a perfect promotional opportunity this was,” Chen Ge grumbled, swiping through the articles. “If I’d known it would go viral, I would have interrupted Captain Yan to advertise the Haunted House! Some of these reports even got the facts wrong. They didn’t include our address!

“Xiao Wan, this is today’s first job. We’ll go through the comments, identify ourselves, and post the Haunted House’s address. Anyone who shows us one of our comments gets twenty percent off!”

“That sounds so unethical…” Xu Wan was embarrassed, but she followed his instructions anyway.

At 9 am, when the park opened for business, both of them put away their phones and prepared to work. After opening the gates, Xu Wan finally saw the Midnight Ticket Counter.

“Boss, did you make this yesterday?”

“Yes, it’s ugly, but it’s usable.”

“It was about time we got a ticket counter.”

At Xu Wan’s solemn expression, Chen Ge sighed inwardly. Such a good employee. She never questions a word I say.

They entered the Haunted House. Xu Wan went to apply her makeup while Chen Ge hauled several planks from the Props Room and barricaded the underground entrance. Until he unlocked new scenarios, the parking lot served no purpose.

Once preparations were complete, they opened for the day. A line had already formed outside the Haunted House. It was not long, even for a holiday, but compared with the old days it was an impressive improvement.

Xu Wan chased visitors through Minghun as the ghost bride, while Chen Ge divided his time between selling tickets and stalking Murder by Midnight as Doctor Skull-cracker. Running the sprawling Haunted House with only two employees was grueling.

Xiaoxiao also staged unscripted encounters in Murder by Midnight. The rag doll liked to trail behind visitors, which worried Chen Ge; one of them might carry her home as a souvenir.

They finally caught a break around noon. Chen Ge checked the black phone. Both his reputation and visitor count had surged, bringing the second expansion within reach.

Two workers managing two scenarios is already at its limit. After unlocking the new scenario, I’ll need to recruit new workers.

Nightmare Missions were often absurdly dangerous, but the Easy and Normal Missions directly exposed weaknesses in the Haunted House. Completing them made the attraction stronger.

Even the phone has issued a recruitment mission… looks like I’ll need to get on that soon.Ever since the old workers that followed Chen Ge’s parents handed in their resignation, he had been wary of hiring new blood. If only Xiaoxiao and Zhang Ya would listen to my commands, they would be the perfect employees.

Of course, it was only a fantasy. Xiaoxiao could probably scare visitors safely, but Zhang Ya would turn the Haunted House into an actual crime scene.

My Team of Ghosts and Ghouls is still empty. I wonder when that will change.Chen Ge sat on the steps outside the Haunted House. He was catching a much-needed breather before throwing himself back into work.

As the sun reached its peak, visitors retreated from the heat and the crowds thinned. Then Chen Ge’s black phone vibrated. The message gave him a start.

“The Midnight Ticket Counter’s effect has been triggered. Your first special visitor has appeared! Seize this opportunity. Your choice will determine the outcome!”

It triggered despite the one-in-a-thousand odds? Given my past experience, this can’t be good!Chen Ge sprang to attention like a soldier preparing for battle and surveyed the area. The sun is blazing. It can’t be a Specter.

The day’s heat had peaked, and noticeably fewer visitors wandered the park.

Is it that couple arguing over there? The girl is so pretty and the guy so ugly—something must be wrong. Who’s Uncle Xu talking to? A new employee? Why haven’t I seen them before?

As Chen Ge speculated, a thin, dark-skinned woman of about thirty approached with light steps.

Could it be her?

Chen Ge silently studied her. She was short, with dark skin, a reserved smile, and a faded jacket.

“Hello. How much is admission to the Haunted House?” The woman’s voice was surprisingly shrill, though not unpleasant.

“We currently have two scenarios; one ticket is 20 RMB, and you can choose which one you would like to experience,” Chen Ge answered with a business smile.

“Okay, then give me two tickets.” The woman handed Chen Ge the money.

“You wish to experience both scenarios?”

“No, one is for him.” The woman smiled apologetically and waved to a boy of eight or nine, who ran over from the shade.

The boy seemed shy around strangers. He stopped beside the woman without taking her hand and stood there expressionless.

“I’m sorry, but the Haunted House has an age restriction. No one under fourteen is allowed inside.” Chen Ge studied the boy. Something about him seemed unusual, though he could not say what.

“Can you please make an exception for us? This boy loves visiting Haunted Houses. There aren’t that many visitors now, so even if we go in, people won’t notice. I promise we won’t cause any trouble.”

“A child that young likes Haunted Houses?” Chen Ge discreetly slipped the black phone into his pocket and shook his head. “I’m sorry, but those are the rules.”
